body:
alex: quick heads-up — seeing a regressed quality signal for llm-llama-13b after the prefetch/scheduler kernel tweak landed in canary. outputs are shifted on long-context evals, truncation looks off :thinking:

maria: ugh. which change? i thought that commit only touched prefetch heuristics for tiled attention. commit: a9f3d2b

jasper: can you paste a tiny repro? i can run locally on mixtral too.

alex: repro is here, run on canary nodes: `python eval_long_context.py --model llm-llama-13b --seq 4096 --batch 8 --canary`

alex: snippet of failing output vs baseline:
```
BASELINE: "...and the meeting adjourned at 5pm."
CANARY : "...and the meeting adjourned at 5pm?"  <-- extra punctuation, shifted tokens downstream
```

perf-bot: perf snapshot (canary vs baseline) — GPU kernel timing (ms): `prefetch_kernel: +0.8ms`, `tiled_attn: -0.12ms`, overall p50 tokens/second: -2.3% on long probes. memory: KV cache hit rate unchanged.

maria: hmm tiled_attn swap + prefetch reorder was meant to reduce tail latency; maybe we introduced a race on KV writeback ordering for odd-head dims. did you repro with head-splitting config?

alex: repro across head configs, but more frequent on models with non-power-of-two kv dim (llama 13b). i can trigger deterministic fail via the eval harness (i'll attach logs).

jasper: can you paste the diff of the scheduler tweak? might be the kernel selector falling back to the latin-path for some batches.

alex: diff: `if (batch_len < prefetch_threshold) schedule_prefetch();` changed to `if (predicted_tail < prefetch_threshold) schedule_prefetch();` — predicted_tail is a moving avg from the estimator.

maria: oh, estimator smoothing may underpredict for certain prompt shapes, causing partial KV writes and a subsequent kernel swap mid-forward. that explains shifted outputs.

sasha: +1 to rollback canary immediately. this is a quality regression, not perf-critical. we can add a conservative canary guard.

jasper: alternatively, add an ordering barrier after prefetch when switching kernel paths. cheap fix: insert `kv_sync_barrier()` before tiled_attn when estimator toggles.

alex: test: adding barrier locally removes shift in 100/100 runs. however adds ~0.4ms per call. perf-bot says overall p50 back to baseline.

maria: thanks — do we have an easy revert? the commit touched two files. i can cut a quick rollback and re-deploy to canary if you want.

alex: please do. i'll open issue with repro, logs, and CI tag. also adding a unit that asserts deterministic KV ordering for head splits.

maria: rolling back canary now — will post new canary ts.

perf-bot: canary rollback completed on canary-3 at 1712349060 — traffic shifted.

alex: reran eval on canary-3 after rollback: outputs match baseline, no downstream token shift. 

jasper: follow-up items: 1) add kv_sync_barrier in kernel selector as a short-term patch; 2) improve estimator smoothing and add safety floor; 3) expand long-context eval suite to include non-power-of-two kv dims.

sasha: filing an incident doc and notifying ops. root cause hypothesis: prefetch_estimator smoothing -> underpred -> kernel-path swap -> partial KV state -> token shift.

alex: ok thanks all. creating rollout ticket to add canary checks for quality regressions tied to kernel swaps + schedule a perf tradeoff review next week. :thumbsup:
